content: The code import Mathlib theorem exple {G} [Group G] (a:G) : a=a := by sorry example : (1:ℝ)=1 := by apply exple raises an error which if I'm understanding correctly is Lean saying it doesn't know how to show that the real numbers form a group; but I've been adding and subtracting and ring_nf ing all over the place until now, so I'm not sure what's going wrong?

R is not a group w.r.t. to multiplication, but with respect to addition. So AddGroup G instead of Group G would work here.

(this is intentional behaviour: If we had an instance Group Real (with addition), one could write a * b but it would really mean a + b, which is obviously suboptimal)

ring_nf works with real numbers because we have an instance Semiring Real if im not mistaken
CommSemiring, remember ring_nf only works with commutative rings
So if I'm trying to apply a result from Mathlib which has [Group G] in its preamble, and I want to use R as my group, is there anything I can do?
usually you will be able to find a corresponding statement for AddGroup
you can also use docs#Multiplicative, which will convert your AddGroup structure on ℝ into a Group structure on Multiplicative ℝ

Also, the reals are a GroupWithZero (docs#GroupWithZero) which is a class that applies to types that are almost groups but have no inverse for 0. There are plenty of lemmas about multiplication that have a GroupWithZero version (usually with a subscript 0, like docs#mul_inv_cancel₀).
